correctness.rationale: The homogeneous word-basis commutator calculation gives rank four for each nonzero degree-one part; with vanishing linear part the rank is the rank of a 2-to-8 quadratic commutator map, equal to one exactly on nonzero squares of linear forms, otherwise two. The central degree-zero and degree-three coordinates contribute nine free dimensions. Counting points on the split Veronese conic establishes q^2-1 nonzero rank-one quadratics. Summing centralizer sizes yields the probability formula. Independently constructed 15-by-15 matrices exhaustively verify noncentral coefficients over F_2,F_3,F_5,F_7. All characteristic-uniform results rely on proof, not finite tests.

value.rationale: The canonical two-generator free nilpotent associative truncation is the first with nonzero degree-three commutators. Its element-centralizer distribution and rank-drop geometry are natural invariants not supplied by generic free-algebra centralizer structure. The nontrivial rank-one locus is an irreducible Veronese-conic cone, giving a motivated complete classification and a closed finite-field commuting probability, rather than a chosen numerical slice.
